preamble: Debuccalization of the voiceless alveolar affricate [ts] to [h], best documented in the Tupi-Guarani family. Proto-Tupi-Guarani had two affricates, *ts and *tʃ; Tupinambá and Old Tupi turned both into /s/, but in the Guaraní subgroup *ts became /h/ while *tʃ stayed a sibilant (*kwetse 'yesterday' > Guarani kwehe, Old Tupi kwese). In the Tenetehara subgroup (Tocantins Asurini, Tenetehára) and in the Kawahíb, Kamayurá and Xingu/Northern subgroups both affricates merged as /h/, later lost in places (Mbya kwee).

examples.note: In Mbya, the *h from *ts is lost word-medially (kwee); Old Tupi has /s/.
In the Guarani subgroup only *ts gave /h/; *tʃ stayed a sibilant (*jatʃɨ 'moon' > jasy).
Tocantins Asurini belongs to the Tenetehara subgroup, where *ts and *tʃ merged as /h/ (*jatʃɨ 'moon' > sahi) independently of the Guarani change.

sources: Carvalho, F. O. de (2022). On the Guaranian evidence for two Proto-Tupi-Guarani affricates. Journal of Language Relationship, 20(1), 81–112. https://doi.org/10.31826/jlr-2022-201-207
